name: Air Fryer Spiced Tilapia with Mango Salsa and Brown Rice

components.name: Spiced Tilapia

ingredients.name: Four raw skinless, boneless tilapia fillets
Fine cornmeal to adhere to fish

steps: In a dry bowl blend cornmeal, paprika, herbs, cumin and salt. Pat each tilapia piece thoroughly dry and rub both surfaces with the seasoning, spraying with measured oil.
Preheat air fryer to 200 C. Air fry fish in one layer, typically 6-10 minutes depending on thickness, until centre reaches 63 C. Keep cooked pieces warm while finishing remaining batches.
Divide brown rice between four containers and add the fish. Pack the mango salsa in separate sealed containers, ideally freshly made for the day you will eat it.
Reheat fish and rice separately and add cold salsa just before serving. The salsa is not suitable for freezing.

components.name: Brown Rice
steps: Rinse brown rice and cook it in measured water until tender, typically 25-35 minutes depending on variety.

components.name: Mango Salsa
steps: Chop mango, red pepper, red onion and coriander; toss with lime and olive oil, then refrigerate separately.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Delish air-fryer spiced tilapia and mango salsa adapted with dry brown rice as full-meal component.
Freezer: fish and rice can be frozen, but texture declines; fresh mango salsa NOT freezer-friendly
Dietary: Fish; cornmeal is gluten-free only if certified.

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder, for 3–4 days at most, and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C and reheat leftovers to at least 74°C.

flags.shelfLife: Fish — plan for days 1-3; the mango salsa doesn't freeze.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or below for 3-4 days maximum; for many fish and shrimp dishes, prioritize eating within 1-2 days for quality and freeze later-week cooked portions promptly.

Cook fish and crustaceans to 63 C (145 F) or applicable local food-safety standard, and reheat cooked leftovers to 74 C. For crab cakes containing egg binder and purchased cooked crab, reheat to 74 C.
When recipe includes rice, cool rapidly and refrigerate promptly; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.
Freeze in suitable airtight food-safe containers. Defrost in refrigerator, not on counter. Re-crisp breading in an air fryer when possible.
Do not freeze fresh avocado, uncooked tomato/cucumber/cabbage salad, or mayonnaise/yogurt-based dressing unless kitchen-tested separately.
Freezer suitability here describes expected eating quality, not laboratory validated shelf life.
